title: The Blackfoot friend plays him Teddy Wilson and changes his life
summary: His friend played him Benny Goodman's trio record with Teddy Wilson, after which Rowles collected Wilson, Basie, Fats Waller, Ellington and Lunceford records.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Oh, he took me under his wing. He said, 'That's not it, Ace.' He said, 'That's not the style to play.' And I was working for my stepfather after school, throwing rugs around, in the Rug Department. And he came up there and he asked if he could borrow me for fifteen minutes. And the old man said 'Yeah.' So he took me downstairs, where they had several... It was a big department store. And there was a record thing there. And they had Benny Goodman's trio record of 'Who?' with Teddy Wilson. And he said, 'Now, sit down and be quiet, and listen to this.' And he put the needle down, and I heard Teddy Wilson.

And my life changed, immediately, right there. I bought all the records they had of the trio records, and then I found the music store and started putting in orders. First thing you know, on order I had all the Teddy Wilson records, then I heard Count Basie, then I had Fats Waller, then I had Duke Ellington, Jimmie Lunceford -- and from then on in, it was mayhem around my house. Billie Holiday singing and everything else. And my stepfather was going crazy, because I wasn't paying any attention to school. All I was doing was trying to learn how to play the piano like that.
